ideas.title: A bottom-bar quick-info widget, with one door anything can speak through
ideas.description:
Antonio, 2026-09-08, after seeing the refused-pick message land in the status bar: the bar should be a proper widget for short-lived information, styled, with a central API so a plugin or any component can put a line there.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, AND WHY IT IS NOT THIS
`AppState.status_note: Option<String>` — added with P082(F003)/T475. A pick with nothing to offer writes one sentence there, `chrome_status` (heca/src/chrome/theme.rs) appends it to the status text, and the next keypress clears it (heca/src/app/input.rs, at the top of `handle_keyboard_input`). It works and it is deliberately plain, but it is:

- **a string on `AppState`, not a widget.** The whole bar is one `Label` built from `format!("{pane_count} panes | {focus_title} | {mode_str}{tail}")`. There is no styling to give a message, no icon, no severity, no room for two things at once, and no way to draw the message differently from the pane count beside it.
- **host-private.** `state.status_note = Some(..)` is reachable only from inside the app. A plugin has no way to say anything there, and neither does a component that is not holding `&mut AppState`. That is the ⭐⭐ RULE ZERO failure: there is no line a plugin author could write.
- **one message, last writer wins.** Two things with something to say silently overwrite each other.

The toast stack was tried first and rejected by Antonio for this case: a key that could not do its thing is not an event worth covering the work with an overlay. So the two are not substitutes — a notification is an *event*, this is a *reply to what you just did*, and they want different surfaces. Whatever is built here must not become a second notification system; see the note on ownership below.

WHAT TO BUILD (to be designed, not decided here)
- A **widget** in `heca-grid-ui` for the bar's transient region: domain-neutral, theme-driven, able to show a short line with a severity and optionally an icon, and to fold to nothing when there is nothing to say (`Visibility` already does the folding — see the rule on its entry in docs/widgets.md).
- **One door to speak through**, reachable from all three surfaces AGENTS requires: the app, a plugin, and RPC. The test is the one in RULE ZERO — write the line a plugin author would type. If it needs a registry, an id, or a host-private type, the API is missing.
- **A lifetime rule stated once.** Today's is "until the next keypress", which suits a reply to a key. A message from a background job wants something else — a duration, or until it is replaced. Whatever the answer, it belongs to the widget or the door, never to each caller: a rule every caller has to remember is the bug.
- **What happens when two things speak at once** — a queue, a priority, or a refusal. Today the second silently wins.

QUESTIONS TO SETTLE BEFORE BUILDING
- Is this the notification system's presentation for a `Toast`-unworthy severity, or a separate channel? Two systems that both put text on screen is exactly the "second path" AGENTS forbids — but a status reply and a notification genuinely differ in lifetime and in who dismisses them. Decide it explicitly rather than by which one gets built first.
- Does the bar keep its current fixed content (pane count | focus | mode) as segments, the way `[appearance.pane] title_segments` already configures the pane info bar? If so this is a segment kind, not a bolt-on, and the whole bar becomes configurable in the same breath.
- Who owns the bar's layout — is it a `ChromeRegion` with children, so a plugin could contribute a segment as well as a message?

WHERE THE CURRENT CODE IS
heca/src/chrome/theme.rs `chrome_status`; heca/src/app/render.rs `status_mode_parts`; heca/src/app_state.rs `status_note`; heca/src/app/input.rs (the clear); heca/src/handlers.rs `pick_refusal` (its first and only caller).

Once the door exists, `pick_refusal` should speak through it like anything else, and `status_note` should go.

ideas.title: A pane's actions and segments are a closed enum — nobody but the host can add one
ideas.description:
Raised by Antonio 2026-09-22 while deciding the region API (P082(F003)/T518). Leave the code as it is for now; this records what is wrong and the shape agreed for the fix.

THE DEFECT
`PaneAction` (Split, MoveLeft, MoveRight, Close, Zoom, Float) and `PaneSegment` (Location, AppName, PaneName, GitBranch, …) are closed Rust enums in `heca-config/src/appearance.rs`. `config.toml` picks from that list BY NAME, which reads like an open vocabulary and is not: a plugin cannot add an action or a segment at all, because there is no variant for it. Adding one means editing the host and recompiling it.

The pane header consumes them in `heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs` — `content.actions` is `&[PaneAction]`, and `pane_action_spec` maps each variant to a glyph, a `WmAction`, a label and a focus rule.

WHY IT IS THE SAME DEFECT AS REGIONS
A fixed list the host owns, selected from by name, with no way for anyone else to contribute. That is exactly what T518 removes for a chrome region. Antonio, 2026-09-22: a plugin or another developer should add a pane action the way a provider is added to a sidebar —

    pane_actions::append(..).prepend(..).remove(..).retain(..)

and the same for segments. Internally that checks what `config.toml` asked for and builds the keys and ids itself, so no caller composes one.

THE ORDER, DECIDED
T518 (the region API) lands first and this reuses its shape — a handle fetched by name, `append`/`prepend`/`remove`/`retain`, placement and `.order` carried by the child, no index methods. Building this before T518 would write the same mechanism twice.

WHAT IT TOUCHES
- `heca-config/src/appearance.rs` — the two enums stop being the vocabulary. A configured name becomes a name, resolved against what was contributed.
- `heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs` — `pane_action_spec`'s match is one contributor among others, not the whole list.
- The identity work in T474: an action's widget key is composed from the pane it belongs to plus the action's name, so a contributed action gets a correct key without its author knowing the rule.

⚠️ Not a licence to start. Propose the task and agree it when T518 is done.

ideas.title: Reusable configurable label segments and action buttons across components
ideas.description:
Captured at Antonio's explicit request as an IDEA ONLY. Implementation is intentionally deferred: this is not approval to implement, promote to a feature/phase/task, or expand P094.

Proposal
Provide reusable components for configured label segments and action buttons that can be composed anywhere: terminal headers, dock views, workspace rows, plugin content, and other surfaces. Register named information/label producers and actions once; each consuming component chooses its own ordered lists through config.toml rather than registration implicitly inserting UI into a universal pane header.

Illustrative configuration from the discussion (provisional names, not an agreed schema):
[settings.pane]
label_segments = ["git", "..."]

[settings.dockview]
label_segments = ["..."]
action_buttons = ["a", "b", "float"]

[settings.dockview.ws]
# Per-component or nested-surface choices.

The exact configuration root remains open: existing visual settings live under [appearance.*]. Do not migrate or add these keys merely because they are illustrated here.

Why
The current extension hooks pane_button, pane_chip and pane_line contribute to fixed built-in chrome surfaces. P094 makes pane content own its own optional header; browser/editor/plugin content may have no header at all. Reusable information and action components would separate the registered capability from its placement, so a consumer explicitly composes the UI where appropriate.

Existing pieces to reuse
- ActionCatalog/ActionRegistry remain the authority for actions, icons, labels, shortcuts, arguments and policy; avoid a competing action registry.
- Tag already renders segmented icon/text labels.
- ButtonGroup already renders grouped buttons.
- pane_items/listing.rs already centralizes configured ordering and default extension contributions.

Open design questions
- Public registration and composition API; names such as SegmentLabels and ButtonActions were suggestions, not decisions.
- How a consumer supplies plain context: which pane/workspace/directory a label reads and which target an action acts on, without host-private AppState or caller-maintained plumbing.
- Applicability and unavailable-data behavior across terminal, browser, editor and arbitrary plugin content; no implicit requirement that a Pane has a header.
- Per-component configuration scopes, reactivity, configuration reload, and compatibility with existing appearance.pane/title_segments/title_actions and appearance.sidebar/pane_lines.
- Native, declarative/plugin and RPC reachability through the established shared paths.

Relationship to existing work
I006 records the narrower original problem of closed pane-action/segment vocabularies; this idea concerns reuse and configurable placement across multiple components, beyond opening that vocabulary. I001 concerns a transient bottom-bar information channel and is separate.
P094(F011)/T450 owns terminal-header ownership; T452 owns generic pane content/creation; T454 proves a second content kind. This idea does not replace, duplicate, block or authorize changes to those tasks. A small rename of existing terminal-header/sidebar hooks was discussed separately, but is not implementation approval contained in this idea.

ideas.title: Table widget on demand for a concrete tabular UI consumer
ideas.description:
IDEA ONLY — preserved from P067(F003)/T253 at Antonio's explicit request on2026-10-29. The original task is closed as canceled; this is not scheduled work, an implementation approval or a prerequisite for P067/P094.

Consider a first-class Table only when an actual application/plugin consumer needs tabular behavior beyond existing composition. Original candidate capabilities: shared columns, a header, row selection and sorting. No concrete consumer was found in the reviewed Heca main/T398 sources. Grid/Row/Label already compose ordinary tables; CardGrid provides selectable cells and navigation, not a complete Table abstraction.

Before promotion, identify the consumer and the exact capability/reuse gap. Agree the public typed constructor/fluent composition and data/event contract; reuse Component, existing layouts/selection and the open host WidgetId/WidgetDefinition registry, never a new closed enum/dispatcher. Include native/described parity, showcase and central docs/widgets.md when a concrete task is approved.

History: T253 was explicitly on-demand and deferred by Antonio on2026-07-25 because its activation condition was not met. On2026-10-29 Antonio approved retaining it as an IDEA and closing the task. Preserve that original task history and link rather than treating the Table as implemented.

ideas.title: Browser pane (CEF offscreen) and embedding arbitrary GUI windows, with the research table
ideas.description:
To be discussed with Antonio one by one. Not approved work. The browser pane was deferred out of v1 on purpose (PROJECT.md:40 out of scope; decision "browser deferred to v2, CEF highest risk", PROJECT.md:64).

Original requirements (.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md:105-107, 116):
- BROW-01: Browser pane renders a real Chromium engine (CEF offscreen)
- BROW-02: Browser pane supports toggling DevTools as a sub-pane or attached window
- BROW-03: Browser pane forwards mouse and keyboard input to CEF
- ADV-01: Window embedding for arbitrary GUI apps (X11 reparenting, Windows SetParent, macOS NSView)

Research, verbatim from .planning/research/STACK.md:28-35 (Browser Plugin v2):
| Approach | Viability | Complexity | Notes |
| CEF offscreen (cef-rs / wef) | High | Very High | Renders Chromium to a shared texture. Cross-platform but ~100MB+ binaries. DevTools supported. |
| Platform WebView (wry) | Medium | High | Creates own window per webview. Hard to composite into our GPU surface without reparenting. |
| OS Window Reparenting | Medium | Very High | X11 XReparentWindow, Windows SetParent, macOS NSView addSubview. Platform-specific, fragile on Wayland. |
Recommendation: CEF offscreen for the browser plugin specifically. OS window embedding as a general plugin protocol for arbitrary GUI apps.

Pitfalls, verbatim from .planning/research/PITFALLS.md:
- #7 (lines 47-52) CEF / Browser Plugin Blocking v1. Warning sign: spending months trying to embed Chromium before the core works. Prevention: Browser is explicitly v2. Do not touch CEF, webviews, or window reparenting until terminal + nvim + tiling are rock solid.
- #9 (lines 59-63) Wayland Window Embedding Complexity. Warning sign: "Window reparenting works on X11 and macOS but is impossible on Wayland." Prevention: Wayland does not allow arbitrary window reparenting. For Linux, prefer X11 for window-embedding plugins, or use xdg-shell surfaces with tight coordination. Document this limitation.

Also .planning/research/FEATURES.md:49-57 lists "Browser pane (Chromium + DevTools): Very High, CEF offscreen rendering or window embedding" and "Out-of-process plugin protocol" as v2.

State today: no code, no planner task. Found by the T561 gap report (M6, M7, K4).

ideas.description:
To be discussed with Antonio one by one. Not approved work. Low priority polish.

Original text: BACKLOG.md:341-352 (terminal-task-01d, locked approach): "(A) integer-row step animated - visible_lines() keeps picking whole rows; the animated value rounds to the nearest row each frame. Zero renderer changes, Q6-safe (Full damage during the animation is fine). (B) sub-row pixel-smooth (renderer shifts content by a fractional row + clips partial rows) is DEFERRED to a follow-up - nicer but needs renderer work. Build A now; revisit B as polish." Only the discrete jumps animate (page up/down, line key, to-top, to-bottom); the wheel applies immediately; rapid scrolls re-target and never queue.
